sources.title: The Rotten Science Behind the MSG Scare | Science History Institute
sources.excerpt: Puzzlingly, though, no two letter writers listed the same symptoms.

reasoning: The claim that MSG causes headaches, numbness, and 'Chinese restaurant syndrome' is misleading. While this belief was popularized after a 1968 letter to the New England Journal of Medicine, decades of subsequent scientific research have debunked it. Rigorous double-blind, placebo-controlled studies have failed to establish a consistent causal link between normal dietary MSG consumption and these symptoms. Additionally, the FDA classifies MSG as 'Generally Recognized as Safe' (GRAS), and the glutamate in MSG is chemically identical to the glutamate naturally present in foods like tomatoes and aged cheeses.
